newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to adopt EU border pact despite opposition.
newsitem.headline: Greece to adopt EU border pact despite opposition.

text.p: The Greek parliament is set to adopt the European Union's Schengen open-border pact on Wednesday despite objections from a number of individual deputies and leftist and religious groups, officials said.

"The Schengen pact will be adopted on Wednesday. Both the ruling socialists and the main opposition conservatives back it. We expect some leaks but it will pass without problems," a parliament official told Reuters on Tuesday.

The agreement, named after the Luxembourg town in which it was signed, came into effect in March 1995. The pact calls for border controls between EU member states to be removed, and for increased cooperation on police matters.
Police used teargas on Monday night to disperse a group of about 1,000 protesters, including Orthodox priests, when they tried to push their way into parliament as the pact was being debated.
Two people were arrested but there were no injuries, police said.
The protesters claim the pact will turn Europe into a giant police state with citizens' personal data available to authorities through a computer network.
A number of countries, including Greece, have passed laws governing limits on the type of information the state can hold on citizens, but debate continues on whether Schengen threatens privacy.

France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Portugal and Germany are all full Schengen members. Greece, Austria, Italy, Denmark, Finland and Sweden have signed but not yet fully implemented the pact.
